text:
- **chief complaint:** the patient presents for an annual exam and follow-up of congestive heart failure, depression, and hypertension.
- **history of present illness:** the patient reports a good low-sodium diet and says they take their medications, though they sometimes forget blood pressure medication. Stress raises their blood pressure. Depression has improved with weekly therapy. Last year's echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of about 45% and mitral regurgitation.
- **physical examination:** blood pressure is mildly elevated in the office. Heart exam reveals a 3/6 systolic ejection murmur. Lower extremities show 1+ pitting edema. Otherwise unremarkable.
- **symptoms experienced by the patient:** nasal congestion from fall allergies. The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, leg swelling, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and thoughts of self-harm.
- **new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages:** lisinopril increased to 40 mg daily. Furosemide (Lasix) 20 mg daily started.
- **follow-up instructions:** repeat echocardiogram ordered. Record blood pressure daily for about one week and report results. Take lisinopril as directed. Schedule a mammogram. Continue low-sodium diet. Take all medications at the same time of day, using an alarm to help remember. Repeat lipid panel this year.
